మరి ఎందుకు ఇంటికి తెస్తున్నారు?
2022 లో Western countries, వేరే దేశాల vaults లో ఉన్న Russia కి చెందిన దాదాపు మూడు వందల billion dollars ని ఫ్రీజ్ చేశాయి.
దాంతో చాలా దేశాలు ఒక పాఠం నేర్చుకున్నాయి... మీ gold మీకు అందే చోటే ఉంచుకోండి.
1991 లో దేశాన్ని కాపాడటానికి gold బయటికి వెళ్ళింది... ఇప్పుడు దేశాన్ని రక్షించడానికి తిరిగి వస్తోంది.
Indian homes are sitting on about 25,000 tonnes of gold.
Now add up the top 10 central banks in the world. America, Germany, Italy, France, Russia, China, Switzerland, even our own RBI, Japan, the Netherlands... Indian homes still have more.
So why do Indians trust gold more than a bank? It's not just tradition. It's math.
Say you put 10,000 rupees into gold in 2006. Today, it's worth about 1.77 lakh. Nearly 18 times.
The same 10,000 in a bank FD, even at a steady 7 percent a year? About 38,000.
Here's the hidden reason. Gold has one price for the whole world. The rupee doesn't. In 2006, one dollar cost about 45 rupees. Today, about 95.
So when the rupee loses value... your gold doesn't. It quietly protects your savings.
And when you need cash fast? Pledge your gold, and the loan comes in minutes, with very little paperwork.
That's why gold loans are now India's second-biggest kind of retail loan, after home loans. About 16 lakh crore rupees.
So the next time your mom, your sister, or your girlfriend buys gold... they're not wasting money.
They're saving it. For the future.

In January, gold hit about $5,590 an ounce. This week? It slipped below $4,000.
That's almost 30 percent gone in nine months. So what happened to the "safest" thing you can own?
Reason one. Gold doesn't pay you anything. A bank FD pays interest. Gold just… sits there.
So when interest rates go up, gold looks less attractive. And in September, America's Fed raised rates for the first time since 2023.
Reason two. Oil jumped on US-Iran tension. Oil up means prices up… and even more fear of rate hikes.
Reason three. When stock markets fall, big investors need cash, fast. And the easiest thing to sell? Gold.
The fast money that rushed in back in January… is now rushing out.
But here's what nobody's talking about. In September, central banks bought about 63 tonnes of gold. The most in almost two years.
So the traders are selling… and the central banks are buying.
And this isn't new. In 2011, gold set a record. It took nine years to beat it, in 2020.
Still, since 2006, it's up about 17 times in rupees.
Gold goes up and down like everything else. That's why people who hold it… think in years, not weeks.

But gold still has a few secrets. Why is an Olympic gold medal… mostly silver? Andhra Pradesh just opened a new gold mine. So why does India still buy almost all its gold from abroad?
